• Mani Ram Canteen. 
One Sunday morning few of us went to canteen for tea. The waiter’s nick name was “Chavanni “. We were waiting for the Tea for a while. Then started raising our voices to Chanvanni to hurry up. By listening our high pitch voice, Mani Ram (the owner) picked up Chavanni’s ear and brought him in front of us. Then, He shouted to Chavanni in High Pitch “Aree, Sahab log Kutte Ke Mafic Bhonk Rahe Hai Aur tu Kan Nahin Dharata” 
We enjoyed the Tea. But realized the sarcastic statement bit later.

participants.name: Jayant Diwakar Muley
participants.career:
I began my career in July 1976 with Gannon Dunkerley & Co. Ltd. (GDC), a professionally managed company of repute specializing in civil and structural works including water & sewage treatment plants, overhead water tanks and chimneys.
During my 30-year tenure with GDC, I worked as Project In-charge on many prestigious projects across India and abroad. Key projects include the 10 Cold Store Project in Iraq, Second Launch Pad for ISRO at Sriharikota, Chennai International Airport, Akash & Agni Missile Projects at Hyderabad, 2x210 MW Power Plant in Bihar and 3x500 MW NTPC Plant at Korba. I was also involved in construction of numerous cement plants, textile mills, pharmaceutical and automobile plants.
From 1995, I served as General Manager-in-charge of Hyderabad and Mumbai Regional Offices, both operating as independent profit centres.
I took early retirement from GDC in 2006 to start my own venture. The initial assignments were civil works for an 80 MW Power Plant for Hindustan Zinc Ltd. at Chittorgarh, a 400 kV Sub-station at Merta and civil & structural works for Uttam Galva Metallics at Wardha.
We undertake works pan-India and have executed projects in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Gujarat. Since inception, the company has consistently attracted sufficient talent to achieve its targeted turnover and revenue. The company is healthy and maintains adequate resources, with a large team of technical, managerial staff and skilled workers engaged across sites to match the requirements.
The journey has been challenging, adventurous and thoroughly enjoyable. I plan to retire at 75 years of age.

My five years of engineering in the hostel were the golden years of my life.
It was a world in itself- a small shared room, common bathrooms ever debated mess food & friendships for a lifetime. 
My close circle- Pawan, Umesh, Guha, Pinaki & many more- we were like brothers. Long late night discussions with endless chai - there was a funny incident every day.

Even after 50 years, when we meet, we become same 20-year olds again.
